title: Generative-AI use is expanding rapidly but remains sharply stratified by country income, connectivity, platform localization and digital capability
source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11231, Who on Earth Is Using Generative AI? Global Trends and Shifts in 2025
geography: Global internet users and country income groups, using traffic to 60 consumer-facing generative-AI tools through mid-2025

denominator.unit: most-visited consumer-facing generative-AI tools tracked in the study

data_source.value: high-frequency website traffic data from Semrush is used to track visits, users and engagement through mid-2025

market_change.value: the tool landscape is rapidly diversifying, with new entrants and multimodal, reasoning and specialized applications appearing during 2025

coverage_limit.value: the study observes consumer-facing web traffic, not all AI use, enterprise deployment, offline use or task-level substitution

observations.method: World Bank working paper using proprietary Semrush traffic data and regression analysis of generative-AI adoption patterns; a verified reproducibility package documents the data and code limitations.
observations.uncertainty: Traffic is a proxy for use and depends on platform access, device, geography, search behavior, bots, subscriptions and unobserved offline or embedded use; some underlying data are proprietary.
observations.subgroup: Internet users, AI-tool users, non-users, platform providers, workers, students, firms and countries with different connectivity, language and income conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Web traffic growth can reflect curiosity or repeated visits rather than productive or consequential use; lower observed traffic may reflect local tools or access routes omitted from the 60-tool frame.

denominator.unit: top consumer-facing GenAI tools in the study's tracked set

chatgpt_share.value: ChatGPT accounted for 77% of traffic to the top 60 tools in April 2025
chatgpt_share.unit: reported share of tracked tool traffic

traffic_growth.value: ChatGPT traffic grew 123% year over year, driven by 42% user growth and a 50% increase in visits per user

duration.value: session duration for ChatGPT doubled over the comparison period

observations.method: Descriptive analysis of Semrush web traffic and engagement metrics for the tracked tool set.
observations.uncertainty: The figures describe traffic concentration and engagement, not revenue, quality, productivity, task completion, labor displacement or user welfare.
observations.subgroup: Consumer-facing AI users, platform providers, advertisers, educators, workers, firms and populations dependent on a small number of dominant tools.
observations.counterinterpretation: High traffic concentration can coexist with intense competition, local alternatives or specialized enterprise use outside the measured consumer-web market.

observations.period: 2025; generative-AI adoption by country income group

denominator.unit: World Bank country income groups compared in the study

high_income.value: about 25% of internet users in high-income countries use ChatGPT

upper_middle_income.value: about 5.6% of internet users in upper-middle-income countries use ChatGPT

lower_middle_income.value: about 3.6% of internet users in lower-middle-income countries use ChatGPT

low_income.value: about 0.3% of internet users in low-income countries use ChatGPT

observations.method: Cross-country comparison of estimated ChatGPT users and traffic relative to internet-user populations, with regression analysis relating adoption growth to GDP per capita.
observations.uncertainty: Income-group differences combine internet access, device and electricity reliability, language, education, prices, trust, local alternatives and measurement coverage; they do not establish a single causal barrier.
observations.subgroup: Internet users across high-, upper-middle-, lower-middle- and low-income countries, with particular implications for students, workers, firms and public institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower use of one global tool may not mean lower AI capability if people use local, embedded, offline, enterprise or open-source systems outside the study’s observed frame.

observations.period: 2025; localization, platform geography and capability inequality

income_gradient.value: regression analysis reports GDP per capita as a strong predictor of adoption growth

localization.value: non-U.S. tools can be highly concentrated in their home markets, including European concentration for Le Chat and very high domestic shares for several Chinese tools

capability_gap.value: the observed global adoption gap implies that access to AI capability may diverge across income, infrastructure and language environments

observations.method: Cross-country traffic analysis, platform-market comparison and regression-based exploration of adoption growth.
observations.uncertainty: The study does not estimate how adoption differences translate into productivity, wages, education, political power or welfare, and the proprietary traffic data constrain independent replication of every underlying estimate.
observations.subgroup: Countries, language communities, local AI developers, platform firms, workers, students, SMEs and institutions competing for digital capability.
observations.counterinterpretation: Localization can reduce dependence on a single U.S. platform and support language fit, but it may also fragment standards, intensify geopolitical technology blocs or create new domestic concentration.

related_sources.claim: World Bank verified reproducibility package describing the Semrush data, 60-tool frame, income-group estimates and proprietary-data limitation.
World Bank Digital Progress and Trends Report resource page listing the working paper.

boundary: This record adds a technology-diffusion and capability-inequality route linking generative-AI web use to platform concentration, country income, infrastructure, localization, language and potential economic participation. It is global traffic-proxy evidence through mid-2025, not respondent-level behavior, complete AI adoption, enterprise deployment, task exposure, causal productivity, labor-market or household-welfare evidence.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official World Bank working-paper PDF, World Bank reproducibility package and Digital Progress and Trends resource page were reviewed for the 60-tool frame, traffic concentration, growth, income-group penetration, localization, regression relationship and proprietary-data limitations.
